mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which may lead to decreased borrowing and spending, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns remain positive more than 50% of the time when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5% indicates labor market weakness, which may lead to economic downturns and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive more than 40% when UNRATE exceeds 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects strong demand in the housing market, which may boost related industries and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns do not show a significant positive correlation with HOUST increases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates increased supply and economic expansion, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth does not correlate with positive 60-day returns, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the unemployment rate is below 4.5%, it may indicate a tight labor market and monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day returns are positive in more than 30% of cases meeting the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) may indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth above 0.5% does not correlate with positive 5-day returns, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS increases) combined with low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 4%) may indicate a Goldilocks economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day returns are not significantly positive when both conditions are met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) below 2% annualized rate may signal economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth below 2% does not correlate with negative 60-day returns, the hypothesis is falsified.
